title: ringswim-waste at 256^2: walled cells from noise swim and divide with no band failure on 3/3 seeds (the 128^2 band is a periodic-box artifact)
summary: The parent claim's world unchanged except a 256^2 domain. On seeds 7, 9, 10 a bounded population (26-35 cells, occupancy 0.18-0.21) of walled cells from noise swims and divides to t=20000: 107-115 persistent splits, generation 14-16, 80-106 track segments >= 3 BL. No seed forms the domain-wrapping band that ended 1 in 5 runs at 128^2 (also at kd 0.06): bands need a head-to-tail chain spanning the periodic box. Reticulate (merges ~0.7 of splits), label-based drive, ring just below the B gate.

claims.statement: At 256^2 on seeds 7, 9 and 10, walled cells that form from noise swim by their own phoretic drift (80-106 segments >= 3 BL, 15-26 >= 5 BL) and divide repeatedly (107-115 persistent splits, generation 14-16), daughters of divisions swimming off, as a bounded population to t=20000.
claims.track: seed 10, celltrack track 604 (strip_s10.png rows 1-3): born by the pinch of 587 at t~11840, swims 6.6 BL as a crescent, divides at t~14540 into 751 and 752
